UN R174.scope_evidence: This Regulation applies to all seating positions in vehicles of categories M and N fitted with safety belt with regard to safety-belt reminders.

UN GTR 9.scope_evidence: This global technical regulation (gtr) shall apply to the frontal surfaces of power driven vehicles

UN R10.reason: The lamp contains LED modules on PCBs and possibly LED driver electronics, wiring and a harness connector. That makes it an electrical/electronic sub-assembly for M1 vehicles, and R10 scope explicitly covers components and separate technical units. Emissions and immunity requirements apply to the PCB and driver design.

UN R148.reason: R148 is the consolidated device-approval regulation for the rear position, stop and reversing lamps. It replaces R7 and R23, which are already removed as superseded. It covers photometry, colour (including lens transmission), reciprocal incorporation of position/stop functions sharing LEDs, and LED light-source provisions. These are the core functions of this product.

UN R150.reason: The product includes a moulded PMMA prism retro-reflector, which is a device type approved under R150 (rear Class IA/IB). R150 replaces R3, already removed as superseded. Its reflectivity, colour and grouping/incorporation provisions apply to this component.

UN R48.reason: R48 is the installation regulation and explicitly lists rear position lamps, stop lamps, reversing lamps and rear retro-reflectors. Its requirements on mounting height and width, geometric visibility angles, colour, grouping/combination and electrical connection (e.g. reversing lamp only with reverse gear and ignition on) constrain the lamp design and its placement at the outboard rear corner of an M1 vehicle.

UN R42.reason: R42 is a whole-vehicle approval for front and rear protective devices (bumper low-speed impact tests). Its only lamp-related clause is a post-test check that the vehicle's lighting devices still work. Whether this lamp is loaded depends on the OEM's bumper and body design, which the spec does not define. Its test procedures and requirements concern the bumper system, not the lamp, so citing it would import many irrelevant requirements. It is handled at vehicle level by the OEM.
